text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet raised by 100 percent the minimum monthly salaries in the public sector and social payments for February.
-- Bulgaria's majority Socialists boycotted parliament in a protest against the agreement on early parliamentary elections. @
-- Two members of Bulgaria's private Trakiabank supervisory council were arrested on charges of siphoning huge amounts of money, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank raised the cash payment limit for traders in the country to five million levs from 500,000 levs.
-- Sofia public transport may stop next week if drivers' demands for a 100 percent pay rise is not met, a trade union official said. @
-- Bulgaria's outgoing Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov said electricity prices should be raised by 350 percent because of the slump of the lev against the dollar.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet raised prices of locally made cigarettes by 100 percent on the average.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet proposed to parliament to raise the monthly untaxable income to 15,000 levs from 3,500 levs.

-- Bulgaria's outgoing prime minister Zhan Videnov appealed to the Socialist party's control commission to expel Nikolai Dobrev from the party on charges of violating party discipline by returning the mandate to form a new Socialist government to the president Petar Stoyanov.
The party's supreme council is expected to discuss Videnov's proposal today. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
